populationSource.note: Current main re-resolved to the same audited 68-QB population across 68 schools before merge.

gradingSemantic: CURRENT COLLEGE FOOTBALL ABILITY AT QUARTERBACK RIGHT NOW; position-normalized; current 2026 performance matters heavily but ordinary one/two-game noise does not erase a stronger established college sample; no NFL projection, recruiting ranking, draft stock, career greatness, fame, school prestige, fantasy value, or future-upside bonus.

evidenceSnapshot.note: The grading evidence is frozen after the Week 4 weekend so games in progress on October 3 do not create inconsistent within-position timing. Prior college seasons remain relevant where the player has an established sample.
primarySources: Official school season-stat and player pages for discrepancy/edge-case checks
Completed-game recaps and box-score context for opponent/role checks

eaDiscrepancyAudit.source: EA Sports College Football 27 current QB ratings, Week 4 snapshot
eaDiscrepancyAudit.rule: Absolute HQ-vs-EA difference of 7+ requires mandatory review; 10+ requires explicit major-red-flag explanation. EA is an error detector, never a formula or midpoint target.

mandatoryReviews.explanation: Keep HQ 87. Florida's current official stats show elite early-2026 efficiency, accuracy and pressure performance; the 78 EA rating is materially behind the demonstrated 2026 level. Short prior sample is already reflected by keeping him out of the 90s.

Keep HQ 96. The user locked Taylor higher after reviewing the anchor board, and the football evidence supports it: through four games he had 1,192 passing yards, 14 TD to 2 INT, plus rushing creation against three Power-conference opponents. EA is functioning as a lag/error detector here, not a ceiling.

Keep HQ 82. Brown opened 4-0 with 68.0% completions, 5 TD, 0 INT and a 91-yard winning drive at Michigan. The prior thin sample prevents an above-average grade, but EA 73 is too low for the demonstrated current level.
Keep HQ 87. His 2026 breakout volume and accuracy are well ahead of EA's 80; the short established sample is why HQ stops at 87 rather than moving into the high-end tier.

postGradeDistribution.note: Distribution was inspected only after player-by-player grading and audits; no grade was moved to manufacture a target shape.

runtimeBoundary: No production/runtime grading behavior is changed by this artifact. It is the locked QB calibration authority for later server-owned Wheel grading integration.
futureVersioning: Any future QB grade change must record previous grade, new grade, effective date, concise reason, and nearby anchor/peer sanity check. Normal maintenance is a targeted exception scan, not a full regrade.
